events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven.** My expected boat rating this week: **Grand Haven 3, Muskegon 2, St. Joseph 2, South Haven 1**. These are my estimates, not DNR ratings, and the newest report is 13 days old.
- **Fish 85-150 ft of water, with lines about 65-100 ft down.** Start with white flashers and green or white flies.
- **Muskegon is the backup**, with spoons and plugs in 90-150 ft of water.
- **Avoid South Haven this week** unless the forecast is calm. Rough water kept boats from the productive depths there.

## Why

- **Grand Haven ranks first:** the Sept 9 Grand Haven report rated boat fishing good, with fish 65-100 ft down in 85-140 ft of water and green and white flies working.
- **I'd expect the cold snap to help the boat bite:** the buoys near these ports dropped 10-17 F in the week before today, a sign of upwelling, and the cooler water should pull salmon shallower.
- **Past seasons back that up:** in mid-September 2023, after a similar 10 F drop, Grand Haven boats rated excellent on glow J-plugs and white flashers.
- **South Haven ranks last:** its Sept 9 boat report was below average, with the best fish beyond 120 ft, where rough water kept most boats away.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest Sept 9, 2026, 13 days old)**
- Grand Haven, Sept 9: boat quality 3 (good); fish 65-100 ft down in 85-140 ft of water; "Green and white flies were effective." Pier quality 0 (slow). (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/4292fc6)
- Grand Haven, Sept 2: boat quality 3 (good); fish 65-130 ft down in 150-220 ft of water; white flasher-fly combinations were effective. (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/4280cb4)
- Muskegon, Sept 9: boat quality 2 (average), "fair numbers" 65-110 ft down in 90-150 ft of water; white flasher with green fly, glow spoons and plugs all worked. Pier was slow because of warm water. (4292fc6)
- Muskegon, Sept 2: boat quality 3 (good); fish 70-130 ft down in 140-200 ft of water; green and blue spoons. (4280cb4)
- St. Joseph, Sept 9: boat quality 2 (average); best bite around 120 ft, with fish about 40 ft down most productive; rough weather limited access to deeper water. The report noted a sharp drop (-4 F) that week. (4292fc6)
- South Haven, Sept 9: boat quality 1 (below average); "rough lake conditions kept most boat anglers from reaching the most productive waters which were beyond 120 feet." (4292fc6)

**Past seasons (history, not current)**
- Grand Haven, 2023-09-13 (surface about 64 F after a 10 F drop): boat quality 4 (excellent) on glow J-plugs and white flasher/flies in the channel and off the pierheads. (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3702b07)
- Similar weeks (surface about 61 F) at the other ports were mostly quality 0-1 for boats, e.g. South Haven 2024-09-11 "slowed due to high waves." These were mostly weaker than the Grand Haven 2023 result.

**Conditions now (live data was unavailable; this is the summary for the week before today)**
- Buoy surface water: St. Joseph 59 F (-11 F over the week), South Haven 61 F (-17 F), Grand Haven and Muskegon 65 F (-10 F). All four show possible upwelling.
- Wind forecast: not returned by the tool, so I can't say what the weekend looks like on the water.

**General guidance (reference, not a report)**
- Michigan Sea Grant/MSU Extension: mature Chinook in early fall hold in or near water of 55 F or less, and upwelling brings salmon toward piers and river mouths.
- NY DEC: Chinook and coho prefer 52-58 F, so salmon hold at the depth where the water is that temperature.

## Caveats

- The newest report is 13 days old (Sept 9). Surface water was 71-72 F then; the buoys now read 59-65 F, so the fish may have moved since those reports.
- Current conditions are a backtest summary, not live readings, and I have no modeled cold-layer depth, so I can't say exactly where the 55 F water sits.
- The ratings above are my expectations based on the sources, not DNR results. Check the wind forecast before going; the Sept 9 reports say rough water kept boats out at all four ports.

## Sources

- Sept 9, 2026 DNR bulletin (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/4292fc6
- Sept 2, 2026 DNR bulletin (Grand Haven, Muskegon): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/4280cb4
- Sept 13, 2023 DNR bulletin (Grand Haven, Muskegon): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3702b07
